why_this_works: Using fattier ground beef (70-80% lean) keeps the meat juicy after draining and gives the spice blend something to cling to. The tomato sauce simmers into the meat and acts as a binder that holds the seasoning in a thin glaze rather than dusty dry spices. Shallow-frying the corn tortillas transforms them from floppy and bland into crisp, toasty shells that hold up under toppings.
notes: Use 70-80% lean ground beef for best flavor. Mexican oregano is key — it's different from Italian oregano.

steps: Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add the ground beef, breaking it up with a wooden spoon. Cook fully until browned and no longer pink.
Drain any excess grease from the skillet. Return to stove and reduce heat to low.
Add the tomato sauce, chili powder, salt, cumin, oregano, granulated garlic, and granulated onion. Stir until the meat is coated in the sauce.
Pour 1/2 cup oil in a medium skillet and heat over medium-high. Test by dipping a tortilla edge — if it sizzles and bubbles, it's ready.
Gently lay a tortilla in the oil and fry each side for about 30 seconds, just enough to add color and crispness.
Remove to a paper towel and carefully fold the tortilla over into a taco shape using tongs or two forks. Repeat with remaining tortillas.
Fill tortillas with taco meat and add desired toppings.
